card: Enables the -Wextra-semi compiler warning flag in CMake and removes redundant semicolons across 65 files. It also adjusts the TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE fallback macro to allow trailing semicolons at invocation points without compiler diagnostics. Importance is low, consisting of internal code styling and compiler hygiene with no behavioral change.
changed_since_previous: The temporary nomerge commit related to libmultiprocess was dropped, reducing the touched files from 67 to 65 across 3 clean commits.
evidence: PR description: "Enable -Wextra-semi and delete all the redundant semicolons."
problem: Extraneous semicolons after member function definitions, namespaces, and macros clutter the codebase and trigger warnings when compiling with `-Wextra-semi`, preventing the warning flag from being enabled project-wide.

risk.why: Mistakes would cause compile-time failures caught immediately by CI rather than runtime bugs.

scope_notes: A wide, mechanical refactoring across 65 files deleting single semicolons, accompanied by a minor macro adjustment and a single-line build configuration update.
summary: Enables the `-Wextra-semi` compiler warning flag in CMake and removes redundant semicolons across 65 files throughout the codebase. It also adjusts the fallback macro for `TRACEPOINT_SEMAPHORE` in `src/util/trace.h` to declare a forward struct rather than expanding to empty space, allowing macro call sites with trailing semicolons to compile without warnings.
